 Judgment

The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Aland (henceforth, referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.518/2016, vide judgment and award dated 05.08.2017.
2. The claimants are the dependents/legal heirs of the deceased Vilas, who was aged 21 years and employed as a mason.
The claimants claimed that Vilas died in a motor vehicle accident on 22.04.2016 when he was hit by a Tractor bearing registration No.MH-25/H-2310 (henceforth referred as 'offending vehicle').

The claimants, therefore filed a claim petition under Section NC:
2023:KHC-K:1351 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The owner and insurer of the offending vehicle were placed ex-parte.
4. Claimant No.1 was examined as P.W.1 and she marked Exs.P.1 to P.9.
5. Based on oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
It also held that deceased Vilas died in the said accident.
It considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month and deducted 50% towards his personal and living expenses and awarded the following compensation.

1. Love and affection Rs.50,000/-
2. Funeral expenses and Rs.25,000/-

4. Medical Expenses Rs.25,200/-
5. Loss of estate Rs.10,000/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, the claimants are in appeal.
7. Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal must have considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.8,750/- per month.
He submitted that the deceased was a mason and a skilled worker and therefore, his income must have been considered at not less than Rs.10,000/- per month.
He further contended that the Tribunal failed to factor loss of future prospects at 40%.

Learned counsel for the insurer did not dispute the fact that in similar circumstances, this Court has considered the notional income of a person dying or injured in a road traffic accident in the year 2016 at a sum of Rs.8,750/- per month.
He also did not dispute the fact that the Tribunal failed to factor loss of future prospects at 40%.
I have considered the contentions urged by the learned counsel for the parties.

The case of the claimants that the notional income must have been considered at Rs.8,750/- per month and loss of future prospects must be awarded at 40% of notional income, is worthy of being accepted.
Consequently, compensation to which the claimants are entitled to deserves to be re-determined as follows:

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.8,66,200/- to Rs.14,44,000/-.
The enhanced compensation shall be paid by the insurer of the offending vehicle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The insurer of the offending vehicle shall deposit the enhanced compensation and interest before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of a receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
If not done, interest for the delayed period shall be recovered from the concerned officer of the insurer.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be kept in the name of claimant No.1 in any Nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
